subject: Agriculture
title: Cover Crops
description: A quick win: understand Cover Crops.

hook.text: Bare soil erodes, bakes, and loses carbon. Cover crops keep the ground clothed between cash crops.

buildup.text: Crimson clover, winter rye, and radishes are planted after harvest—not for sale, but for soil protection.

discovery.text: Cover crop roots hold soil, suppress weeds, and feed microbiological life during the otherwise dead off-season.

twist.text: Only 5% of US cropland uses cover crops despite proven benefits. They cost money and yield nothing directly.

climax.text: Government payments for cover cropping are increasing—treating soil health as a public good worth subsidizing.

punchline.text: Crops you don't sell protect the soil that grows crops you do.

quiz.question: What percentage of US cropland uses cover crops?
